items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: He had, uh, Pop Foster on the bass. Uh, he had Pop Foster's brother Willie Foster on the violin. That's it.

ctx.x: And you remember who else was in the band with Oliver when you worked with him and where

you played? Uh, let's see now. We played so many different, we was playing spot job. We didn't have no sound plays until we went to Hunson Nagel. Now, uh, let's see. What color was this, Hunson Nagel? He had, uh, Liberty in the Outerville. Liberty. He's band, he had, uh, uh, Call it the Casino. Oh yeah. He had, uh, Chris Kelly. Uh, no, uh, he had, uh, uh, Chris Miner on the drum. And he had, uh, uh, Alphonse Piku. And, uh, Joe Atkins. Uh, Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Ed Atkins. Ed Atkins was, yeah.…
That was the Magnolia band. Do you remember, uh, I think, uh, Louie Kepard tells me that he played in the Magnolia band too with Oliver for a while.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I played violin with him... And, uh, he had Willie Foster playing violin.

ctx.x: Yeah, I played violin with him, you know. I didn't stay with him long. And, uh, he had Willie Foster playing violin. That's George Foster's brother.
We got him up in Baton Rouge, remember Ralph?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Joe Oliver had, he had Louis Kepard on the guitar, Pop Foster on the bass, and Willie Foster on the violin... when I was playing with, uh, with, uh, what you call him, uh, Joe Oliver

ctx.x: What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is…

Olavon and Wooden Joe. Yeah, well, no, he had a whole band. Oh yeah, he had a whole band? Joe Oliver had a whole band. Mm-hm. Celestane. Joe Oliver had, he had Louis Kepard on the guitar, Pop Foster on the bass, and Willie Foster on the violin. That was Pop Foster's brother. And, uh, that's the, uh, the famous clarin, uh, clarinet and saxophone, uh, hot dog.
Where did he die? The clarinet play, is that the one that went up north or stayed here?
